channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Canadian Dollar recovers as softer US Dollar offers relief ahead of US CPI
item.description: USD/CAD falls around 0.45% on Tuesday as US Dollar (USD) bulls take a breather ahead of Wednesday’s US inflation report.

item.title: Dollar Index slips from its 18-month high before US CPI
item.description: The September Consumer Price Index (CPI) is due on Wednesday at 12:30 GMT, with headline inflation forecast to rise to 3.6% from 3.4%. Core prices, which leave out food and energy, are forecast up 0.2% in the month against 0.6% overall.

item.title: British Pound finds fresh momentum as BoE hawks set stage for US CPI
item.description: The Pound Sterling registers gains against the US Dollar on Tuesday, up 0.28% as investors seem confident that the Bank of England (BoE) will raise rates at its November meeting, while they brace for the release of US inflation figures. The GBP/USD trades at 1.3244.

item.title: Neither a breakout nor a reversal: What OCBC, Commerzbank and ING expect from the US Dollar
item.description: Three banks agree the US Dollar (USD) is on solid footing for now, but none expects a decisive breakout or a sharp reversal soon. OCBC, Commerzbank and ING credit the Greenback's support to higher Oil prices, firm US yields and sticky Federal Reserve (Fed) tightening expectations.

item.title: Taiwan Dollar: Monetary tightening and housing recovery – DBS
item.description: DBS economist Ma Tieying expects the Central Bank of the Republic of China to raise its policy discount rate by 12.5bp to 2.125% in December as CPI stays above 2% and electricity price risks build.

item.title: Euro finds support from softer US Dollar, French fiscal risks linger
item.description: EUR/USD gains ground on Tuesday as the US Dollar (USD) retreats from recent highs, giving the Euro (EUR) some breathing room despite persistent concerns over France’s fiscal and political outlook. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1192, up 0.33% on the day.

item.title: British Pound: Upside momentum builds against Euro – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists note EUR/GBP has continued its pullback after failing at the 0.8610 graphical hurdle linked to the February and March troughs. The cross has slipped below the July lows, reinforcing prevailing downside momentum.

item.title: Gold struggles to reclaim $4,200 as Fed interest rate hike risks persist, US CPI looms
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) reverses earlier gains on Tuesday as US Treasury yields recover after falling earlier in the day. With the US Dollar (USD) still under pressure, the metal trades little changed during American trading hours.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Modest gains against US Dollar - Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret reports the Canadian Dollar (CAD) up 0.2% versus the US Dollar (USD) but underperforming other G10 currencies, with markets still pricing Bank of Canada (BoC) tightening into year-end despite weak labour data.

item.title: Australian Dollar : Key support at 0.6935 in focus against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report AUD/USD slipping as the stronger US Dollar weighs on commodity currencies. Short‑term momentum has turned lower, with scope for a test of major support at 0.6935, though a sustained break is seen as unlikely.

item.title: Australian Dollar edges higher amid softer US Dollar, hawkish RBA
item.description: AUD/USD edges higher on Tuesday as a pullback in US Treasury yields weighs on the US Dollar (USD), pulling it away from recent highs. Meanwhile, hawkish signals from the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) provide underlying support to the Australian Dollar (AUD).

item.title: Indian Rupee: RBI defense limits losses against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale's strategists note that the INR has rallied further, with USD/INR looking to break below the 95 handle as the RBI intensifies its FX defense. The central bank extended FX curbs to GIFT City and broadened use of risk reserves.

item.title: US Dollar: Supported but capped by CPI risks – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong argue the US Dollar (USD) remains supported by higher Oil prices, firm US yields and resilient Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations, but not yet breaking out of its recent range. They note markets are focused on energy, US inflation and earnings, with a decisive USD move likely requiring a meaningful upside surprise in core CPI. The base case is for a supported but range-bound USD.

item.title: Euro: Lower year-end target at 1.13 against US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole writes that EUR/USD is moderately undervalued versus short-term fundamentals, reflecting a persistent France-related risk premium that could widen if French bonds sell off further. He sees a challenging backdrop for Euro bulls, expects a possible test of 1.110, and notes that ING has revised its EUR/USD forecast down to 1.13 for the fourth quarter of 2026 and first quarter of 2027.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA inflation focus shapes outlook – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur explains that the Reserve Bank of Australia is increasingly focused on high inflation, with trimmed-mean inflation above its 2–3% target band for over a year.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Weakness may deepen toward 159.05 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note USD/JPY continues to grind higher as wide US‑Japan yield differentials weigh on the Japanese Yen (JPY). Intraday, the pair is expected to hold within 158.20–158.80.

item.title: US ADP Employment Change 4-week average drops to 24.75K
item.description: Private-sector hiring in the US has gained some pace in late September. According to the NER Pulse, the weekly companion to the ADP National Employment Report, companies added an average of 24.75K jobs per week in the four weeks ending September 26.

item.title: Copper: El Niño risks cap African supply growth – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Commodity Compass, authored by Michael Haigh and Jeremy Sellem, highlights how El Niño 2026-2027 could constrain copper output in the African Copperbelt.

item.title: EUR/GBP Price Forecast: Downtrend remains firm despite deeply oversold RSI
item.description: EUR/GBP reverses earlier gains on Tuesday as fiscal and political concerns in France limit the Euro’s (EUR) upside, while the technical picture also suggests sellers remain dominant.

item.title: Indian Rupee: RBI measures support near term – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Michael Wan analyses recent Reserve Bank of India actions and their impact on the Indian Rupee. He notes that RBI’s new FX and liquidity measures have sharply strengthened spot USD/INR, but also pushed stress into forwards, offshore NDFs and bonds.

item.title: British Pound: Firmer ground with BoE hike risk – ING
item.description: Francesco Pesole at ING highlights a supportive backdrop for the Pound, with EUR/GBP now expected to trade in a 0.84–0.85 range for several months as Euro-specific risks persist and the Bank of England signals readiness to hike. While ING sees BoE expectations as too hawkish for 2027, one or two hikes look increasingly likely, and the budget risk is seen as manageable for Sterling.

item.title: WTI Oil extends its pullback to $91.00 amid US imports of Russian Diesel
item.description: Crude Oil trades lower on Tuesday, as investors ponder the impact of the US President, Donald Trump’s decision to lift the ban on Russian diesel imports.

item.title: Indian Rupee extends gains on RBI's fresh measures
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) extends the Monday’s advance against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, driven by the announcement of fresh Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) US Dollar-related measures to shore up the domestic currency.

item.title: Australian Dollar remains weak despite hawkish RBA minutes
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) trades lower against its major currency peers, except the US Dollar (USD), during the European trading session on Tuesday. The antipodean is under pressure even as Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) minutes of the September policy meeting remains hawkish.

item.title: Brent: Uptrend intact with $114–116 in sight – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale technical analysts highlight that Brent has been consolidating sideways after meeting an interim hurdle near $110 in September. The contract remains above its 50-day moving average around $97, keeping upward momentum intact. Brent is now testing a short-term descending trend line, with potential objectives at $110 and $114/$116, while the recent $102 low acts as first support.

item.title: US Dollar: Higher rate expectations support gains - Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Thu Lan Nguyen discusses how the US Dollar (USD) reacted to Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s move away from traditional forward guidance.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: looking for direction between 209.00 and 210.00
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) retraces previous losses against the Japanese Yen (JPY) on Tuesday, and returns to the mid-range of the 209.00s after bouncing from lows at 208.90 earlier in the day.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD wobbles near $60.30, US CPI takes centre stage
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) trades in a tight range at around $60.30 during the European trading session on Tuesday. The white metal consolidates as investors shift their focus to the United States (US) Consumer Price Index (CPI) data for September, which will be released on Wednesday.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Stronger footing with intervention risk – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes that the Japanese Yen has firmed modestly, pulling USD/JPY back toward 158.00 and keeping it below the 200-day moving average near 158.50.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Range consolidation persists against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank (UOB) strategists Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/CHF has rebounded but still lacks strong upside momentum. In the near term, they see the Dollar trading in a slightly higher 0.8320/0.8355 band, while over the next 1–3 weeks they expect a narrower 0.8295/0.8365 range. On a 1–3 month horizon, they see continued rebound but not a retest of the July peak.
